subject: POC scope change & next steps - AcmeCorp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmecorp.com>, Peter Luo <peter.luo@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: POC scope change & next steps - AcmeCorp

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned as we kick off the POC.

What we heard (summary):
- Primary objective: reduce time-to-insight for customer support reps by surfacing relevant KB articles and suggested response drafts.
- Secondary objective: extract structured attributes from support tickets for routing and analytics.
- Current constraints: must process PII-lite dataset, SLA for inference latency <= 350ms p50 for 1-2k concurrent users during the trial.

Proposed POC (baseline):
- Use case A: Response drafting (generation + retrieval). Success = 70% helpfulness by Acme rubric (survey + blind eval).
- Use case B: Attribute extraction (NER + classification). Success = 85% F1 on sampled tickets.
- Duration: 4 weeks of active evaluation after data ingestion.
- Owners: Redwood (Marissa/PS) to deliver infra + test harness; Acme (Sarah/Peter) to provide 10k sanitized tickets and evaluation rubric.

Attachments: POC_success_criteria.xlsx (success metric templates), draft_SOW_Acme_2026-11.pdf (SOW + milestones).

Open items / ask:
1) Can Acme confirm ownership for data prep and who will be the technical contact for ingestion (SFTP or S3)?
2) Are you ok with the proposed success thresholds above, or do you want to adjust before we lock the baseline?
3) We flagged the possibility of adding an ingestion/normalization use case mid-trial — if you foresee that being necessary, please indicate now so we can allocate the infra.

Next steps:
- Sarah/Peter: confirm data contact and any redlines on the SOW by Friday 11/27.
- Redwood: schedule kickoff once data contact confirmed; provide ingestion checklist and shared Drive folder.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite once we have data contact.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Peter Luo <peter.luo@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC scope change & next steps - AcmeCorp

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A couple of items from our side:

1) Ingestion owner: we'll have our Data Ops lead (cc'd to security@acmecorp.com) handle the S3 transfer. I'll confirm the exact contact and credentials by EOD Monday.
2) Success thresholds: the response helpfulness target looks fine, but for attribute extraction we'd like to add an additional metric — precision at top_k for entity extraction, because false positives are costly for routing. Can we add "Precision@top1 >= 88%" to the criteria?
3) We also want to add an ingestion/normalization step to the scope: normalize timestamps and map legacy category codes before running extraction. We understand this is a scope change and may require a short re-baseline.

Timeline-wise, adding the normalization step likely shifts the active evaluation window by ~1 week. Can Redwood confirm impact on test harness and whether that requires extra engineering time?

Also attaching our internal security contact for SOC questions — security@acmecorp.com.

Thanks,
Peter
Senior PM, Customer Success | AcmeCorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmecorp.com>, Peter Luo <peter.luo@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: POC scope change & next steps - AcmeCorp

Team — forwarding Peter's note. Key asks: add normalization use case (timestamps + category code mapping) and add Precision@top1 >= 88% to extraction success criteria.

Proposed internal plan:
- Camila: can we absorb the normalization step with minimal engineering work by leveraging the ingest pipeline + a small preprocessor? Estimate: 3 engineer-days to add mapping + tests.
- Lauren: we may need to shift the active evaluation window by 7 days; suggest we keep total calendar from kickoff + ensure SLOs are still reachable. If engineering effort requires a change to SOW, I'll surface to legal.
- I'll coordinate updated success_criteria sheet and circulate to Acme for sign-off.

I'll propose a 30-minute re-baseline call with Acme early next week to confirm.


Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmecorp.com>, Peter Luo <peter.luo@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC scope change & next steps - AcmeCorp

Marissa — confirmed. We can handle the normalization preprocessor. Details:
- Implementation: small Lambda job that runs during ingestion to apply timestamp normalization & category mapping table (mapping file to be provided by Acme).
- Estimate: 3 engineer-days total (1 engineer for 2 days + 1 QA/ops day).
- Impact on timeline: move active evaluation start by 7 days. New proposed schedule: kickoff 12/14, data ingest and validation 12/14-12/18, active eval 12/21-01/15 (4 weeks active).

Attached: poc_plan_v2.docx (includes updated timeline and owners).

Action items for Acme: please upload mapping file and sanitized tickets to the shared Drive link. Also confirm that Precision@top1 >= 88% is acceptable as an additional success metric.

Thanks — happy to jump on the re-baseline call if needed.


Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
